He drove the tractor into a pond between the Washington Monument and Vietnam Veterans Memorial, threatening to blow it up with bombs. Watson had operated a 1,200-acre family tobacco farm for five generations but was hit by drought and had his crop quota cut in half. After 36 hours of careful listening, FBI agent Winnie Miller recognized Watson was deeply Christian. The negotiators mentioned that the next morning was the Dawn of the Third Day, allowing Watson to surrender honorably.
